blocks.text: Swann Galleries Fall offering of Fine Photographs is set for Thursday, October 15, 2026.

Notable works from the nineteenth century include Francis Frith’s The Pyramids of Dahshoor, from the East , 1857 ($6,000-9,000); and a rare daguerreotype by Felix Jacques Moulin, Two Prodigal Women , 1860s ($7,000-10,000). The auction further features a significant constructivist composition by Alexander Rodchenko, Pushkin Square , 1932 ($20,000-30,000), and a rare portfolio by Todd Webb previously unoffered on the market ($18,000-22,000).

Further highlights include imagery of the American West with Ansel Adams’ Winter Sunrise, Sierra Nevada from Lone Pine, California , 1944, printed April 1978 ($30,000-45,000), and Moonrise, Hernandez, New Mexico , 1941, printed 1963-70 ($30,000-45,000); and abstraction studies, including ten photographs from the Seaweed Martha’s Vineyard Portfolio , 1943-53, printed 1982, by Aaron Siskind ($7,000-10,000).

The auction also features works associated with the Kamoinge Workshop, including Gordon Parks’ American Gothic , 1942, printed circa 1970 ($6,000-9,000), and Roy DeCarava’s Man Coming Up Subway Stairs , 1952 ($12,000-18,000).

Street photography features Fan Ho, Three Men Walking, Hong Kong , 1962, printed 2006 ($7,000-10,000); and Elliott Erwitt’s oversized Arc de Triomphe, Paris , 1956, printed 2000s ($10,000-15,000). Contemporary highlights feature Peter Hujar’s Keith, N.Y. , 1981 ($10,000-15,000), and Vik Muniz’s Aftermath (Emerson) , from the Children of Brazil project, 1998 ($8,000-12,000). Fashion photography includes images by Richard Avedon, Bruce Weber, Helmut Newton and more.

A selection of press photographs documenting civil rights by Bob Adelman with No Man is an Island, Kelly Ingram Park, Birmingham, Alabama (Civil Rights demonstrators) , 1963, printed 1970s ($4,000-6,000), and Fred McDarrah with George McGovern and Coretta King, Political Campaign , 1972 ($700-1,000), along with examples of vernacular photography, will further enrich the dynamic sale.
Bidding is available through online platforms, absentee, the phone, and live in-person. Live online bidding platforms will be the Swann Galleries website, Invaluable, and LiveAuctioneers.

Swann Auction Galleries is a third-generation family business as well as the world’s largest auction house for works on paper. In the last 80 years, Swann has repeatedly revolutionized the trade with such innovations as the first U.S. auction dedicated to photographs and the world’s only department of African American Art. More than 40 auctions and previews are held annually in Swann Galleries’ two-floor exhibition space in Midtown Manhattan and online worldwide. Visit swanngalleries.com for more information.
